newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhs may sell Bulgaria 100,000-300,000 T grain.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhs may sell Bulgaria 100,000-300,000 T grain.

text.p: Kazakhstan may sell Bulgaria 100,000-300,000 tonnes of grain in coming months, a Bulgarian diplomat in the Kazakh capital of Almaty said on Wednesday.
"The final amount of grain will depend on its quality," Iordan Trenchev, Bulgaria's charge d'affaires to Kazakhstan, told Reuters.
A Bulgarian government delegation visited Almaty earlier this week, seeking a possible grain deal.
A Kazakh official told Reuters that the grain might be delivered through the Kazakh Agroindustrial Exchange at average prices but could provide no further details.
Kazakhstan's minimum export price per tonne of wheat is $165.
Bulgaria will run out of its own grain reserves before the new harvest, the Kazakh official said.
Bulgaria was offering to pay for the Kazakh grain by taking part in construction projects in the town of Akmola in central Kazakhstan, which authorities have designated the country's new capital.
Trenchev said Kazakhstan owes Bulgarian construction company Glavbolgarstroi $30 million for a hospital it has nearly built in the Kyzyl Orda region in southern Kazakhstan.

Kazakhstan harvested 11.6 million tonnes of grain from its vast steppes last year, and Kazakh Deputy Prime Minister Zhanybek Karibzhanov has said his country could export five to six million tonnes of grain.
